key_insight: Physics-guided machine learning can prescreen point defects in 4H-SiC by predicting formation energies and zero-phonon lines quickly enough to accelerate high-throughput defect discovery.
engineering_relevance: The approach can reduce expensive DFT relaxations in defect screening workflows, helping prioritize candidates for power electronics and quantum-device applications.
method: Compared ridge, kernel ridge, and multilayer perceptron models.
Used three defect descriptors for single and double point defects in 4H-SiC.
Targeted prescreening predictions without the costly relaxation step typical of ML interatomic potentials.
evidence_signal: For vacancies and substitutions, the best models reached MAEs of 0.437 eV for formation energy and 0.202 eV for ZPL; for interstitials, errors were higher at 1.101 eV and 0.230 eV.
watch_item: Performance is notably weaker for interstitial defects, so the models are best viewed as a screening tool rather than a full substitute for detailed DFT characterization in all cases.
paper_title: Prescreening Point Defects in Semiconductors With Machine Learning
